edges.description: Generalized ulceronecrotic papules rapidly coalesce into large ulcers in FUMHD.
High fever accompanies the ulceronecrotic eruption and is a defining FUMHD feature.
Systemic inflammation in FUMHD can be complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation.
Extensive cutaneous ulceration and systemic involvement predispose to sepsis, the leading contributor to FUMHD mortality.
Cutaneous barrier loss and systemic involvement culminate in sepsis in fatal FUMHD.
The clonal-TCR arm is a parallel modifier that shifts a subset toward worse outcomes and higher mortality rather than causing sepsis directly.

nodes.description: Because sepsis of the denuded skin is the dominant cause of FUMHD death, antimicrobial therapy and aggressive wound care / infection control are outcome-determining and are counted among the successful FUMHD modalities.

nodes.description: FUMHD lesions, like PLEVA, contain increased CD8-positive and TIA-1-positive T cells; in severe cases the dermal and subcutaneous infiltrate can be atypical CD8-positive with features of lymphomatoid (angiocentric) vascular injury. The cytotoxic phenotype is proposed to drive keratinocyte injury and ulceronecrosis, though function is inferred from tissue immunophenotype.

nodes.description: A subset of FUMHD cases harbors a monoclonal (clonal) T-cell receptor rearrangement in the lesional infiltrate, placing those cases on a continuum with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) and predicting a worse prognosis. This is a parallel modifier arm, not present in all cases, and whether it marks a distinct neoplastic subset or a transient reactive clone is unresolved.

nodes.description: TNF-alpha inhibitors (e.g., infliximab, often with IVIG) are reported for refractory FUMHD and are mechanistically rational given the elevated serum TNF-alpha at the PLEVA-to-FUMHD transition. Response is not uniform - at least one infant died despite a TNF-alpha inhibitor - so this remains a case-based option, not established therapy.

nodes.description: FUMHD is the severe branch in which generalized ulceronecrotic papules coalesce into ulcers while high fever and systemic inflammation develop. Systemic manifestations include disseminated intravascular coagulation and pulmonary, cardiac, gastrointestinal, and central nervous system involvement; the extreme end can meet HLH criteria. The molecular reason only a minority of PLEVA patients enter this branch is unknown.
